name: Traffic Purple
lede: Traffic Purple is a deep reddish purple from the German RAL signage standard, and almost never a match in old paintings.

sections.title: A signal purple
sections.body:
RAL, founded in 1927, lists this hue as RAL 4006, a screen approximation of a spec that RAL issues as physical chips, so it will shift between displays [1]. When the number was added to the register is undocumented here [1]. Maerz and Paul separately recorded a very close tone in 1925, under the name Monsignor, on plate 41 K8 of their 1930 dictionary [1]. The two names come from different systems for different uses, so their closeness looks like coincidence rather than borrowing [1].

The nearest named neighbor in our library is [[flirt]], 2.9 units away and more vivid [2]. [[amaranth-deep-purple|Amaranth Deep Purple]] follows at 4.0, a touch redder, and Crayola's [[violet-crayola|Violet]] sits at 4.6, duller [2]. RAL also lists [[telemagenta]], RAL 4010, a pinker and lighter signal color in the same 4000 series [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this hue, as photographed, in only 2 of 23,781 paintings, rarer than 82 percent of the named colors we track [2]. Both are works dated about 1900 in the Cleveland Museum of Art's collection [2]. The sample is too small here for century, painter or company statistics [2].

Editor spot-audit 2026-10-09: 'first recorded 1927' and Telemagenta 'from the same 1927 standard' unsupported (RAL founded 1927; RAL 4010 is a much later addition), now undocumented; Flirt distance was 7.1 (Plum's curriculum distance), graph says 2.9; Flirt is 'more vivid', not 'pinker, less red'; 'darker and more saturated than red-purple' false (red-purple #E40078 is far more vivid), removed; speculative 'restored paint' line replaced with what the two hits are.
